Georgia State's explosive rushing offense meets a Coastal Carolina defense that allows explosive rush plays (+1.94).

Georgia State owns the stronger opponent-adjusted scoring matchup: Georgia State offense vs Coastal Carolina defense +1.23, Coastal Carolina offense vs Georgia State defense -0.10 (points per game, opponent-adjusted: Georgia State offense #27 of 138, Coastal Carolina defense #93 of 138).
3 independent volatility indicators are present: this matchup has wide outcomes.
Coastal Carolina's defense has forced turnovers at a high rate (+1.54 SD) while allowing average-or-worse yards per play: takeaways are regression-prone.
Georgia State's offense has given the ball away at a high rate (+1.14 SD). Regression-prone: reported as volatility, never as a cause on its own.
Georgia State's leading passer in its last game (Ayden Pereira) is not its season leader (Cameran Brown): season passing numbers may not describe the quarterback who plays.

pace.definition: possession_environment = (z of home offense plays + z of away defense plays allowed + z of away offense plays + z of home defense plays allowed) / 2, on adjusted values. volatility.definition: offense_ypp_residual_sd = game-to-game spread of the offense's yards per play around what the fit expected against each opponent; its percentile is within the FBS universe. explosive_yard_share_z is the raw share standardised across FBS (not opponent-adjusted). takeaways_per_game_z and giveaways_per_game_z are RAW per-game turnover counts standardised across FBS: turnovers are regression-prone and are deliberately not opponent-adjusted.
